meta.requirement: Explore Springvale (5%+ exploration) to trigger this quest.

customTabs.label: tip
customTabs.content:
You can click the '''Collapse''' button and the '''Best Route''' → '''Important Only''' button at the top to minimize it.
''Some quests will not have a Best Route choice, because the best choice is subjective or not yet found.''

You can also click the '''Endings''' button at the top to view all possible endings, and clicking an ending will show the options needed to reach that ending.

start.title: Ducks Downtown
start.text:
''Near the small pond at the edge of Springvale, you spot a boy no older than ten sitting on a rock and sobbing so hard he can barely breathe. An empty wooden coop sits open beside him.''

Oliver: ''sniffles'' W-Wadsworth... where are you...?

ruok.text: Oliver: ''looks up with red, puffy eyes'' N-no I am NOT alright, stranger! My duck is GONE! Wadsworth has been missing since this morning and nobody cares and I have looked EVERYWHERE.

turnup.text:
''Oliver stares at you, lip trembling''.

Oliver: Turn up? TURN UP?! Wadsworth is not a misplaced sock! He is my best friend and companion of SEVEN YEARS. You are not very helpful, stranger.

Who_is_Wadsworth.text: Oliver: Wadsworth came to me when I was three years old. My uncle brought him as an egg. I watched him hatch. I named him. I have hand-fed him bread every single morning for seven years. He knows my voice. He follows me to school. ''voice cracks'' He is my BEST FRIEND.

choices.label: I'll help you look for him

helplook.text: Oliver: ''wipes his nose on his sleeve'' You mean it? Oh, thank you, stranger! His feathers are white and brown. He is quite fat because I feed him very well. He makes a sound like -- ''ahem'' -- BWAAAK. Not like other ducks. He is very distinguished. Perhaps ask around town?

dialogues.speaker: 📌 Objective
dialogues.text: Ask the townspeople of Springvale about Wadsworth the duck

continues.label: Do /rpg again and click ask the townspeople button

askrpsing.text: ''You begin asking around Springvale. The villagers have mixed opinions about Wadsworth''.

choices.label: Ask the farmer near the field

askfarm.text: Bram the Farmer: ''looks up from his hoe'' That fat duck? Gone, is he? ''mutters'' About time. Seven years that bird has been waddling into my cabbage patch. I found him in there just yesterday morning, sitting on my best turnip like it was a throne. Good riddance, I say.

choices.label: Did YOU do something to him?
Did you see where he went?

didudosmth.text: Bram: ''splutters'' ME?! I am a farmer, not a duck murderer! I shoo'd him out of my field and went back to work. Now take your suspicions elsewhere before I set my dog on you.

oldwom.text:
''An elderly woman named Elsa is knitting by the well. She lights up when you mention the duck''.

Elsa: Oh, yes! That dear fat duck! I always give him bread on my morning walk. Lovely creature. This morning I saw those Rook boys, you know the ones, the older lads from the east side. They had a cage. Headed up the main road toward Mondstadt. I did think it strange.

choices.label: The Rook boys? Who are they?

rookboi.text: Elsa: A handful, those three. Older than young Oliver by a few years, maybe thirteen or fourteen. They call themselves his friends but I have never trusted them. Always looking to make a quick Mora. ''lowers voice'' Word is they have been gambling on marbles again.

lesgoogambaaa.text: Elsa: ''nods gravely'' Very serious business around here. Lost a fortune in marbles myself back in '92. But I digress. If those boys headed toward Mondstadt with a duck, I would check the market district, dear. Someone may have seen something.

dialogues.speaker: 📌 Objective
dialogues.text: Follow up on the lead in Mondstadt City

Fine__What_did_you_see_.text: Bram: Saw a group of boys over by the old mill road carrying something in a cage. Heard a noise that sounded very much like -- ''he pauses'' -- BWAAAK. Thought nothing of it. Boys will be boys.

choices.label: Ask the old woman by the well

travmond.text:
''You arrive in Mondstadt City and begin asking around the market district. Most people shrug. Then, near the Good Hunter tavern, you notice a handwritten chalkboard sign by the entrance.''

''It reads: "Today's Special: Crispy Roasted Duck Confit, served with seasonal herbs. Fresh from Springvale!"''

''Your stomach drops''.

good_hunt.text:
''Sara, the cook, is beaming with professional pride''.

Sara: Welcome! You are just in time. I got the most wonderful duck this morning. Very fresh. Came from some boys out of Springvale. Fat little thing, lovely feathers. I have never heard a duck make that particular sound before. Very distinctive.

choices.label: Did the duck have a name?

whtsnd.text: Sara: ''cheerfully imitates'' BWAAAK. Like that! Very unusual. Anyway, he is in the oven now --

namedyck.text: Sara: A name? ''laughs'' I did not ask. I bought him from three boys for fifty Mora. They seemed very eager to sell. Very, very eager. ''she pauses'' Why do you ask?

His_name_was_Wadsworth.text:
Sara: ''expression falls'' Oh. Oh no.

''An awkward silence hangs over the kitchen. The smell of roasting duck drifts in from the back.''

Sara: I am so sorry. I did not know. The boys said he belonged to their uncle. ''She hands you a crumpled receipt: "Springvale Boys x3, 1 live Pekin duck, 50 Mora''."

''Fifty Mora. Wadsworth was sold for fifty Mora. They probably spent it on marbles''.

dialogues.speaker: 📌 Objective
dialogues.text: Return to Springvale with what you have learned

rtrnwithwhatlrn.text:
''You return to Springvale. Oliver is still by the pond, clutching a piece of bread he saved for Wadsworth's breakfast. A short distance away, three older boys sit on a fence, snickering and counting small coins.''

Oliver: ''looks up with hopeful eyes'' Did you find him? Did you find Wadsworth?

choices.label: Tell Oliver that Wadsworth flew away to a beautiful pond

confrontbois.text:
''You walk toward the boys on the fence. They tense up immediately. The oldest one, Thomas, crosses his arms''.

Thomas: What do you want, stranger?

You: I just came from the Good Hunter in Mondstadt. Had a very interesting chat about a duck.

showrcpt.text:
''You hold up the crumpled receipt. Thomas goes pale. The other two boys look anywhere but at you''.

Thomas: Look, we just thought... he was always around and we --

You: Fifty Mora. You sold your friend's duck. His companion of seven years. For fifty Mora.

Thomas: ''very small voice'' We already spent it.

onwhatmf.text:
Thomas: ...Marbles.

''A long pause.''

Thomas: ...And some toffee.

''Another pause.''

You: You are going to fix this. Springvale market has a livestock stall. You will pool whatever Mora you have left and buy Oliver a new duckling. Right now. I will be watching.

choices.label: Walk with them to the market

buynewduck.text:
''Twenty minutes later, the three boys stand before Oliver, holding a small wooden box with air holes poked through the lid. From inside comes a very small, very confident sound: BWAAAK.''

Thomas: ''staring at the ground'' ...We're sorry, Oliver. We did something bad.

Oliver: ''stares at the box'' ...Is that a duck?

wadsworth2.title: Wadsworth II
wadsworth2.text:
''Thomas opens the box. A tiny duckling blinks up at Oliver with great seriousness.''

Oliver: ''whispers'' ...Oh.

''He reaches in and the duckling immediately waddles onto his palm.''

Oliver: He makes the same sound. ''looks up at you, eyes wide'' Can I name him Wadsworth?

''You nod. Oliver looks back down.''

Oliver: Hello, Wadsworth. I am Oliver. I have been waiting for you.

''Thomas and his friends slink away in quiet shame. The toffee was not worth it.''

tellolivtruth.text:
''You crouch down to Oliver's level. There is no good way to say this.''

You: Oliver... Wadsworth was taken to Mondstadt. Those boys over there sold him to a cook. I am so sorry.

dotdotdot.text:
''Oliver stares at you. His face does not move for a very long time.''

Oliver: ...Sold him?

''The bread falls from his hand.''

Oliver: They SOLD him?

''He turns and looks at the boys on the fence. They notice. One of them starts to whistle innocently.''

Oliver: ''very quietly'' ...Those are my friends.

ending_mqvri311.title: The Whole Truth
ending_mqvri311.text:
''Oliver stands up. He is very small. The boys are much bigger. None of that appears to matter to him right now.''

Oliver: THOMAS ROOK, YOU SOLD MY DUCK!

''He charges at them like a cannonball. The boys scatter in three different directions, screaming. The whole village turns to watch.''

''You stand by the empty coop, holding a crumpled receipt for fifty Mora, and say nothing.''

wadsflew.text:
''You look at Oliver's tear-streaked face, at the bread in his hand, at the empty coop''.

''You think of Sara's kitchen. Of the chalkboard sign. Of fifty Mora''.

You: I found out what happened. Wadsworth found the gate to the old mill road on his own. He waddled all the way to a beautiful pond outside Mondstadt. He seemed very happy. Very free.

dot3.text:
Oliver: ''sniffles'' A pond? A real pond?

You: Big and clear. With lily pads. He was swimming in circles and making that BWAAAK sound at the fish.

Oliver: ''small laugh through tears'' He always did that to our fish pond too.

''He stares out toward the fields for a long moment.''

Oliver: ...As long as he is happy.

fuckingliar.title: A Merciful Lie
fuckingliar.text:
''You walk away. Oliver sets the bread down on top of the empty coop, a small offering to a duck that will never come home''.

''Behind you, the Rook boys have heard everything. The oldest one catches your eye and gives you a slow, smug smile''.

''You keep walking''.
